contract.kernel_domains: DOMAIN (which declarations exist) comes from the AOT kernel, the conservative choice. ABI comes from the PRE-AOT kernel, because --aot strips parameters: topLevel(int x) reads req=1 pre-AOT and req=0 after, so two different declared signatures erase to the same empty shape and an AOT-derived ABI over-claims. BODY is combined from both and counts as changed if EITHER moved.
contract.independence: abi_fingerprint is built from signature nodes and body_fingerprint from a walk of the function body. Neither is derived from the other.
contract.incumbent: incumbent_printed_sha256 is printed Kernel as build_patch.dart computes it -- a reference ORACLE for cross-checking, never the contract, and not an input to either fingerprint.
body_exclusions: source positions (fileOffset, file URIs) -- incidental source metadata
local variable NAMES, encoded by binding ordinal instead -- a local name is not observable (justified by g2_local_rename)
body_non_exclusions: statement and expression ORDER -- execution order is observable (g2_stmt_order)
abi_exclusions: type-parameter NAMES, encoded by position and bound -- not observable at a call site (justified by g2_typeparam_rename)
contract.abi_shape: States the ROADMAP P2 refusal boundary in the map itself: named, optional-positional and type arguments are refused before publication, so the map says so rather than classifying them reusable.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Shape.area
results.note: the METHOD is unchanged. Whether the owning class's layout change makes the method unsafe to reuse is a SEPARATE question owned by SM1-G5, and must not be smuggled into the fingerprints.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::usesPrivate
results.note: corpus.helper::_privateHelper and corpus.app::_privateHelper share a simple name across privacy domains; a map that confuses them will report app's caller as changed

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::usesPrivate
results.note: JUSTIFIES body exclusion #2. A local's name is not observable, so encoding locals by binding ordinal is safe. Compared against g2_local_base rather than base, because base writes the member as an arrow expression with no local at all -- comparing against it would measure a shape change, not a rename.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::usesPrivate
results.note: PROVES order is NOT excluded. Execution order is observable, so the body fingerprint must move. If this case reported body_equal the canonicalizer would be discarding something that changes behaviour.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box
results.note: JUSTIFIES the ABI exclusion. A type parameter's name is not observable at a call site; position and bound are what a caller depends on.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::pick
results.note: The body walk used to start at f.body, so formals never entered the local table and every reference encoded as VarGet#-1 -- making `=> a` and `=> b` identical. Formals are now registered in declaration order, and an unregistered variable is a refusal rather than an ordinal.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::topConst
results.note: The field body used to record only whether an initializer existed, so `final x = 1` -> `final x = 2` stayed equal. The initializer expression is now encoded.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Shape.square
results.note: Initializer lists are separate Kernel structure and are not reachable from function.body, so this change vanished entirely. Constructors now encode c.initializers.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box.unwrap
results.note: G1 deferred the owner/type relationship here. Box.unwrap's own signature is unchanged, so its ABI is equal -- but reuse still must be refused, because the owner's ABI moved. The row carries owner_abi_fingerprint and the classifier requires BOTH to match.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::looped
results.note: The refusal must be REACHABLE and expected, not merely representable. The classifier returns refused:unsupported_body before any equality check, and reuse requires BOTH baseline and variant encodings to be supported -- an unsupported baseline is just as disqualifying.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::Box.unwrap
results.note: app's Box is UNTOUCHED, so its member's owner ABI must not move. With the owner table keyed by bare class name, corpus.other's Box overwrote corpus.app's and this member would inherit the wrong contract.

results.subject: package:corpus/other.dart::Box.unwrap
results.note: Same class name, same member name, different library: this one's owner ABI must move. The pair only passes if the owner table is library-qualified.

results.subject: package:corpus/app.dart::looped
results.note: reversed direction: the BASELINE is the unencodable side. classify() originally read only the variant's body_status, so an unencodable OLD body compared against a clean new one would have been classified on body equality. Reuse compares two encodings; either being incomplete makes 'equal' mean 'equal in the parts I looked at'.
